prompts.display_text: Pin a country where ground was broken for a new temple in 2022.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country where ground was broken for a new temple in 2022.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and milestones, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: A groundbreaking starts construction of a temple, usually a few years after it is announced. 16 temple groundbreakings were held in 2022 in 7 countries or territories; see each answer for the temple and date.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Grand Junction Colorado (16 April 2022); Lindon Utah (23 April 2022); Farmington New Mexico (30 April 2022); and 7 more.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Torreón Mexico (10 December 2022).

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Bahía Blanca Argentina (9 April 2022).

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Miraflores Guatemala City Guatemala (3 December 2022).

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Lubumbashi Democratic Republic of the Congo (20 August 2022).

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: Managua Nicaragua (26 November 2022).

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: Freetown Sierra Leone (19 March 2022).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1958 and 1962
prompts.text_original: Between 1958 and 1962 the Church organized its first stakes in a run of countries far from Utah, a sign that Saints abroad were being asked to build Zion where they lived. A country whose first stake of the Church was organized between 1958 and 1962.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (New Zealand, England, Australia, Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, Samoa, Mexico)
prompts.note: Mexico does not count: its first stake, in the Chihuahua and Sonora colonies, came in 1895. Canada's also came in 1895.
prompts.summary: After New Zealand received its first stake at Auckland in 1958, stakes followed in Manchester, England and Sydney, Australia on the same day in 1960. Rotterdam, Berlin and Zurich gained the first stakes in the Netherlands, Germany and Switzerland in 1961, and Apia, Samoa followed in 1962.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: The Manchester England Stake, the first in Europe, was organized March 27, 1960.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: The first stake in Australia was organized in Sydney, March 27, 1960.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: The Berlin Germany Stake, the first in Germany, was organized September 10, 1961.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: The first stake in New Zealand was created in Auckland, May 18, 1958.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: The Zurich Switzerland Stake, the first in Switzerland, was organized October 27, 1961.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Holland Stake, the first in continental Europe, was created at Rotterdam, March 12, 1961.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: The first stake in the Samoan Islands was organized at Apia, Western Samoa, March 18, 1962.

prompts.display_text: Pin a non-Soviet Warsaw Pact country (today's borders) dedicated or rededicated for the gospel between 1977 and 2006
prompts.text_original: As communist rule eased and then ended, Church leaders dedicated or rededicated the former Soviet satellites of Europe for the preaching of the gospel. A country that was a Warsaw Pact member other than the Soviet Union (Poland, East Germany, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Albania), in its present-day form, dedicated or rededicated for preaching the gospel between 1977 and 2006.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Poland, Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Albania)
prompts.note: Germany does not count. Elder Nelson's 1990 Prague rededication counts for the Czech Republic; Slovakia had its own in 2006.
prompts.summary: Spencer W. Kimball rededicated Poland in 1977 while it was still communist. Russell M. Nelson dedicated Hungary in 1987, then Romania and Bulgaria and rededicated Czechoslovakia in early 1990. Dallin H. Oaks dedicated Albania in 1993, and Dieter F. Uchtdorf dedicated newly independent Slovakia in 2006.

answers.name: Poland
answers.fact: President Spencer W. Kimball rededicated Poland in Warsaw, August 24, 1977.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson rededicated Czechoslovakia in Prague, February 6, 1990.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Hungary on Gellert Hill, Budapest, April 19, 1987.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Romania in Cismigiu Park, Bucharest, February 8, 1990.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Bulgaria in Sofia, February 13, 1990.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: Elder Dallin H. Oaks dedicated Albania at Monument of Heroes Park, Tirana, April 23, 1993.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf dedicated Slovakia in Trencin, May 12, 2006.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a nation made to drink the wine cup of fury in Jeremiah 25 (leave out Arabia)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a nation or city made to drink the wine cup of the Lord's fury in Jeremiah 25:17-26 (Jerusalem and Judah, Egypt, the Philistine cities, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, Zidon, Elam, the Medes, and Sheshach); Dedan, Tema, Buz and Arabia are left out because their extent is unclear
prompts.note: Gaza (Azzah) is in Palestine; Ashkelon, Ekron and Ashdod are in Israel. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: Jeremiah is told to take the wine cup of the Lord's fury and make every nation drink it, starting with Jerusalem and ending with Babylon under the cipher Sheshach. Between them come Egypt, the Philistine cities, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Zidon, the kings of Arabia, and Elam and the Medes (Jer 25:15-26).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Pharaoh king of Egypt, his princes and all his people drink the cup (Jer 25:19).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The cup begins with Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, and includes Ashkelon, Ekron and Ashdod (Jer 25:18, 20).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Edom, Moab and the children of Ammon drink it (Jer 25:21).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The king of Sheshach, a coded name for Babylon, drinks after them all (Jer 25:26; compare Jer 51:41).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: All the kings of Tyrus and Zidon drink it (Jer 25:22).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: All the kings of Elam and of the Medes drink it (Jer 25:25).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Azzah, which is Gaza, is among the Philistine cities named (Jer 25:20).

prompts.display_text: Pin a former Soviet republic an Apostle dedicated or rededicated for preaching the gospel between 1990 and 1993
prompts.text_original: As the Soviet Union opened and then broke apart, Apostles dedicated or rededicated several of its former republics for the preaching of the gospel. A former Soviet republic, in its present-day borders, that an Apostle dedicated or rededicated between 1990 and 1993.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (Estonia, Russia, Armenia, Ukraine, Latvia, Lithuania, Belarus); Church News 1993
prompts.note: Georgia (1999), Moldova (2001), Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan (2003) were dedicated later, so they do not count.
prompts.summary: Between 1990 and 1993, as the Soviet Union opened and then dissolved, five Apostles dedicated or rededicated seven of its former republics. Elder Russell M. Nelson prayed over Estonia and Russia in April 1990 and Belarus in 1993; Elders Oaks, Packer, Faust and Ballard dedicated Armenia, Ukraine, Latvia and Lithuania.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson rededicated Russia in Leningrad's Summer Garden, April 26, 1990.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: Elder Boyd K. Packer dedicated Ukraine in Kyiv, September 12, 1991.

answers.name: Estonia
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Estonia near Tallinn, April 25, 1990.

answers.name: Armenia
answers.fact: Elder Dallin H. Oaks offered the prayer dedicating Armenia in Yerevan, June 24, 1991.

answers.name: Lithuania
answers.fact: Elder M. Russell Ballard dedicated Lithuania in Vilnius, February 20, 1993.

answers.name: Latvia
answers.fact: Elder James E. Faust dedicated Latvia at Jurmala, March 17, 1993.

answers.name: Belarus
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Belarus in Yanka Kupala Park, Minsk, May 11, 1993.
